references.text: Abraham will surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him
and in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed, because you have obeyed my voice
I will make your offspring as numerous as the stars of heaven and give to your offspring all these lands. And in your offspring shall all the nations of the earth be blessed
Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you

Your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth, and you shall spread abroad to the west and to the east, to the north and to the south. And in you and your offspring shall all the families of the earth be blessed
Blessed is everyone who blesses you, and cursed is everyone who curses you
May his name endure forever; as long as the sun shines, may his name flourish. In him shall all nations be blessed; let them call him happy
You are sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham: 'And in your offspring shall all the families of the earth be blessed'
The Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham: 'In you shall all nations be blessed'
Balaam's confirmation that God's blessing or curse is an unavoidable reality based on the Abrahamic covenant.
Applies the principle of the covenant in a personal prayer that the enemy's curses should turn into blessings.
Contrasts the retributive logic of the Abrahamic covenant with the new covenant ethic of actively blessing enemies.
Affirms the judgment aspect of the Abrahamic covenant: God's retribution against those who oppress His people.
Affirms the judgment aspect of the Abrahamic covenant: God's protection of His people by putting their enemies to shame.
Affirms the judgment aspect of the Abrahamic covenant: God's protection of His people by destroying their enemies.
Affirms the judgment aspect of the Abrahamic covenant: God's protection of His people by destroying their enemies.
Fulfillment of the Abrahamic Covenant: God's people move from being a curse to becoming a blessing for all nations.
Affirming the spiritual dimension of the Abrahamic Covenant: God's outpouring of the Spirit upon Abraham's offspring as part of the blessing.
Theological interpretation of the Abrahamic Covenant: Those who believe are blessed together with Abraham, fulfilling the promise that all peoples will be blessed.
Theological interpretation of the Abrahamic Covenant: The blessing to Abraham comes to the Gentiles in Christ, fulfilling the promise that all peoples will be blessed.
